Maintenance Report — MNT-0145-005

Asset: WELL-0145 (NE-07 Well 145, T350, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 08 Jul 2023 08:00 · Finished: 18 Jul 2023 05:00 · Well stopped for this job: 237 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Daniel Foster Triggered by: inspection INS-0145-0037 on 2023-07-06 Report written: 19 Jul 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that the motor breaker kept tripping and the pump jack would not run. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0145-0037 showed the wellhead at 37.7 °C with the air at 33.7 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit. The well stayed shut in for about 8 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

Root cause

Moisture got into the motor terminal box and damaged the windings.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Disconnected and removed the motor.
  2. Fitted the exchange motor on the existing base.
  3. Aligned the sheaves and tensioned the belts.
  4. Checked rotation direction and motor current.

Summary of the fix: replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours; motor current within the nameplate rating and stroke rate normal. The well was returned to production.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0145-010

Asset: WELL-0145 (NE-07 Well 145, T350, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: flowline Work started: 23 Feb 2024 08:00 · Finished: 24 Feb 2024 04:00 · Well stopped for this job: 20 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Daniel Foster, Kevin Price · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0145-0067 on 2024-02-22 Report written: 26 Feb 2024

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0145-0067 at 14:45 on 2024-02-22 found crude oil on the pad: about 11.1% of the pad area, estimated 5.1 bbl. The inspector noted: "Dark staining on pad." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 8.6 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Thread fatigue from pump jack vibration.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 2% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.
  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 360 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 288 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 3.9 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0145-010 (WS-06).
  • 4 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.4% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0145-021

Asset: WELL-0145 (NE-07 Well 145, T350, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: flowline Work started: 19 Dec 2025 08:00 · Finished: 14 Jan 2026 17:00 · Well stopped for this job: 633 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Brian Coleman, Kevin Price Triggered by: inspection INS-0145-0158 on 2025-12-18 Report written: 16 Jan 2026

What happened

Field staff reported that a damp, dark patch appeared along the flowline route. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0145-0158 showed the wellhead at 15.9 °C with the air at 12.3 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Excavation found a corrosion pinhole on the bottom of the line. The well stayed shut in for about 24 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

Root cause

External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 0% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the leak.
  2. Cut out the corroded section.
  3. Welded in a new section of line pipe.
  4. Coated the new joint.
  5. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: cut out and replaced the corroded flowline section.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 360 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 288 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Waste
